title: Study of quantum turbulence by vortex-antivortex dynamics in dipolar BECs
abstract: We investigate vortex nucleation and dynamics in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate stirred by a rotating Gaussian obstacle. Two stirring protocols are compared: continuous stirring with constant amplitude (Case 1), and obstacle removal at $t = 15$ ms with linear amplitude ramp-down (Case 2). In both cases, a smooth angular velocity ramp ($t_{\text{acc}} = 3$ ms) suppresses spurious phonon excitations. The first vortex pairs exit the obstacle at $t \sim 3$ ms, and by $t \sim 8$ - $10$ ms the individual vortices and antivortices are fully resolved in the phase maps. Case 1 yields a vortex population that grows up to $t \sim 40$ ms and then roughly saturates, while Case 2 yields a population that peaks around $t \sim 15$ - $25$ ms and then decreases. Remarkably, both protocols lead to local triangular-like ordering in selected regions of the condensate by $t \sim 50$ ms, exhibiting clear dipolar signatures: elliptical distortion and elongated vortex cores along the polarization axis. The mixed vortex-antivortex population remains stable up to $100$ ms with no observable annihilation, indicating that dipolar interactions strongly suppress vortex decay. Kinetic energy decomposition confirms that incompressible (vortex) energy dominates at late times. These results establish a controlled platform for vortex studies in dipolar superfluids and provide benchmarks for future experiments on quantum turbulence with long-range anisotropic interactions.
summary: This paper numerically investigates quantum turbulence in dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates by analyzing vortex dynamics under two different stirring protocols. The key findings demonstrate that dipolar interactions stabilize vortex pairs against annihilation and induce local crystalline ordering. The results establish a controlled theoretical benchmark for future experimental studies on anisotropic quantum fluids.
main_problem: The study investigates vortex nucleation, dynamics, and the resulting quantum turbulence in dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs).
main_result: The research shows that dipolar interactions strongly suppress vortex-antivortex annihilation, and both stirring protocols lead to local triangular ordering with clear dipolar signatures.
method: Numerical simulations solving the time-dependent Gross-Pitaevskii equation using the split-step Crank-Nicolson method.
model_or_system: The system is a dipolar BEC, modeled by the GP equation, and is subjected to controlled stirring via a rotating Gaussian obstacle potential. The study compares continuous stirring versus controlled obstacle removal.
key_observables: Vortex population dynamics, local triangular ordering, kinetic energy decomposition ($E_c$ vs $E_i$), and the energy spectrum $E_i(k)$ adherence to Kolmogorov scaling.
important_parameters: The study uses specific parameters for dipolar interactions ($a_{dd} = 131 a_0$) and compares two stirring protocols (constant amplitude vs. linear ramp-down).
main_assumptions: The use of a smooth angular velocity ramp ($	ext{tacc} = 3$ ms) is employed to suppress spurious phonon excitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate column-density and phase evolution for both stirring cases, and show the time evolution of total, compressible, and incompressible kinetic energy components.
paper_structure: The paper compares two stirring protocols (Case 1: continuous stirring; Case 2: obstacle removal) to study vortex dynamics, analyzing energy spectra and vortex stability over time.
why_interesting: This work provides a controlled, theoretically modeled platform to study quantum turbulence in systems with long-range anisotropic interactions, which is crucial for understanding superfluid dynamics in dipolar quantum gases.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (Color online) Column-density evolution for a dipo- lar BEC continuously stirred by a rotating Gaussian obsta- cle (Case 1). Parameters: N = 2.5 × 104, as = 100 a0, add = 131 a0, A0 = 300 ℏωρ, σ = 0.7 ℓρ, r0 = 6.5 ℓρ, ν0 = 1.0 rad/ms, and tacc = 3 ms. The 5×3 panels correspond to t = 0.5, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, and 100 ms. Vortices appear as dark density holes. The first vortex pairs exit the obstacle at t ∼3 ms, becoming visible in the t = 4 ms panel. By t ∼50 ms, local triangular-like ordering develops in selected regions of the condensate, rather than a globally ordered lattice. Insets in the t = 40 ms and t = 50 ms pan- els show the vortex positions...

FIG. 2. (Color online) Phase evolution corresponding to Fig. 1 (Case 1). Vortices appear as 2π phase dislocations. The phase maps confirm nucleation at t ∼8-10 ms, a disordered phase at 20-40 ms, and gradual ordering into a triangular vortex lattice by t ∼50 ms.

FIG. 3. (Color online) Column-density evolution for a dipolar BEC in which the rotating Gaussian obstacle is re- moved at t = 15 ms (Case 2). The amplitude ramps linearly, A(t) = A0(1 −t/15) for t ≤15 ms, and is zero thereafter; all other parameters are as in Fig. 1. The first vortex pairs exit the obstacle at t ∼3 ms and proliferate during the stir- ring phase (t ≲15 ms). After obstacle removal, the vortex array evolves freely. By t ∼50 ms, local triangular-like or- dering emerges in selected regions of the condensate, with- out the formation of a globally ordered lattice. No decay of the vortex population is observed up to 100 ms. Insets at t = 40 ms and t = 50 ms show the vortex...

FIG. 5. (Color online) Time evolution of the kinetic en- ergy components for (a) Case 1 (continuous stirring) and (b) Case 2 (obstacle removal at t = 15 ms). Black solid curves: total kinetic energy (EK). Blue dashed curves: compress- ible kinetic energy (E(c) K ), associated with sound waves and phonons. Red dotted curves: incompressible kinetic energy (E(i) K ), associated with vortex motion. The vertical dashed line at t = 15 ms in panel (b) marks the obstacle removal time. The smooth angular velocity ramp (tacc = 3 ms) is ac- tive in both cases for t < 3 ms.

FIG. 4. (Color online) Phase evolution corresponding to Fig. 3 (Case 2). Phase singularities nucleate before t = 15 ms and persist after obstacle removal. The free evolution allows the vortex ensemble to rearrange into an ordered lattice by t ∼50 ms, as confirmed by the regular arrangement of 2π phase dislocations.
